(2) Q3 2026 results, date not yet announced; the Q2 report came 2026-08-12, so a report around 2026-11-10/12 is likely but may fall just outside the window. Q3 guide is core revenue $214-216M (only ~2-3% q/q), so the print itself is low-bar; the swing factor is the 2027 outlook ('more than triple revenue') and any clarity on OpenAI's use of Cerebras after the unconfirmed SemiAnalysis report that GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast runs on Nvidia GPUs. Lock-up supply and negative momentum (stock -52% from first close) argue for a small negative drift; sharp prior declines and a possible strong 2027 guide argue for reversal. Net: median ~$146 (-2%), log-sd ~26% for the month (realized vol is IPO-inflated at 115%; peers ~70-85% annual; plus an earnings event).

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 18.7x (NVDA) to 107x (ARM), median 45.4x over the 9 peers with a forward P/E (CRWV, NBIS have none). Forward P/S 2.2x (CRWV; ~4.6x EV-based) to 40.8x (ARM), median ~12.3x over 10 peers (TSM forward P/S on the page is a data error). comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 6.5x NTM EV/sales sits inside the peer range, between the two neoclouds (CRWV ~4.6x, NBIS 7.65x) and well below the chip-peer median (~12-14x). 18x NTM EV/EBITDA is below every peer's trailing EV/EBITDA. A P/E is not used: Cerebras is GAAP loss-making through 2027.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to chip peers is structural and should persist through the horizon: (a) ~70%+ of revenue and most of the $25.4B RPO is one customer (OpenAI), whose MRA runs 3-4 years (max 5) and allows termination of late capacity; (b) the business is now mostly cloud capacity at ~41% core gross margin (Q2 2026) vs 60-75% at chip peers, with depreciation-heavy economics like CoreWeave/Nebius; (c) the company says it needs significant additional capital; (d) Nvidia's Groq 3 LPX (in full production) targets the same SRAM-based low-latency decode niche and SemiAnalysis notes Cerebras has no near-term path to more on-wafer SRAM. The slight premium to CRWV reflects own silicon (gross-margin upside), net cash instead of heavy debt, and higher NTM growth at the horizon.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$98 the diluted equity is ~$29.5B; less the net cash still expected at the horizon after heavy capex, EV would be roughly 4-5x my FY2028 revenue - a CoreWeave-level multiple on revenue that would already assume the OpenAI ramp falls short. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental broke (OpenAI capacity cuts or delays, loss of the Ultrafast/latency tier to Nvidia, a FY2027 outlook well below 'more than triple', or a deeply dilutive raise) rather than ordinary volatility.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine finds the horizon multiples (6.5x NTM EV/sales, 18x NTM EV/EBITDA) imply a WACC of 14.3%, close to my 14.8% built from a 2.29 peer beta. Put differently, paying ~$123 at the horizon requires FY2029 revenue ~$7.2B (OpenAI RPO plateau ~$5.5B/yr plus ~$1.7B non-OpenAI), GAAP EBIT ~20%, and an exit at 14x EBITDA (~$47B EV at end-2029), i.e. the market must believe OpenAI renews or is replaced after 2030. Given the 35% probability I put on non-renewal, 14x (below CRWV 23.5x / NVDA 27x trailing) already carries a ~$14/share haircut; the current $148.86 implies roughly the consensus 2027 path ($2.95B) plus partial option exercise, so the market is pricing somewhat more than my base.

reasoning: Lane: industry/value chain. Facts: FY2025 revenue $510M (86% UAE customers); Q2 2026 core revenue $209.9M, core GM 41%, RPO $25.4B (mostly OpenAI 750MW, 22% recognized by mid-2028, 43% over the next 24 months); FY2026 core guide $880-890M and 'more than triple' 2027; consensus FY2027 $2.95B. Net cash ~$7.7B, ~301M diluted shares (incl. options, RSUs and vested OpenAI warrants). Value chain: demand is strong across neoclouds (CoreWeave backlog $104B, Nebius growing fast), but competition in Cerebras's niche is hardening - Nvidia's Groq 3 LPX is in full production with Nebius/CoreWeave as first customers, SemiAnalysis argues Cerebras lacks a path to more on-wafer SRAM, and SemiAnalysis said OpenAI's newest Ultrafast tier runs on Nvidia GPUs (unconfirmed; the stock fell ~9% on it). Positives: AMD (Helios+WSE, Q4 2026) and AWS (Bedrock, Q1 2027) partnerships validate the decode role; Cerebras avoids HBM/CoWoS bottlenecks. OpenAI's own compute plan was cut to ~$600B through 2030, which caps upside from the 1.25GW option. Valuation: DCF, EV/NTM sales (6.5x, neocloud range) and EV/NTM EBITDA (18x) all give ~$123 at the horizon; heavy capex (system cost ~$13M/MW) and dilution are the drags. Scenarios $65/$123/$246 at 25/50/25 (ladder uses ~38% within-scenario log-vol, model set 35%); I nudge the centre slightly toward the market price because of model uncertainty, giving a median ~$128 and P(>= today's $149) ~40%. Base rates: AI-infra peers move +/-50-70% a year; the stock's realized vol (115%) is IPO-inflated, so I use ~75-85% effective vol. One month: final lock-up expiry (~Nov 9) and Q3 results (~Nov 10-12, unconfirmed) - slight negative drift, wide spread. Research limits: several pages (Benzinga lock-up schedule, Business Chief Altman quote, DCD UAE export, Blockspace Nebius) returned 403 and are not cited; X posts were not fetched directly.

Core gross margin 41% (Q2 2026) with operating leverage on ~$6-7B revenue; neocloud peer CoreWeave still posts GAAP losses on interest, so 20% GAAP EBIT is set below the chip-peer level and reflects cloud economics with depreciation in COGS.
H1 2026 D&A $42.6M on $373.5M revenue (11%); rises as capex on CS-3 systems (SemiAnalysis BOM ~$450k per CS-3 rack) is depreciated over ~5 years.

H1 2026 capex $548.9M (147% of revenue); >600MW live/contracted by end-2027 at ~$13M/MW system cost (SemiAnalysis BOM ~$450k/CS-3 rack, ~25kW wafer) plus AMD Helios racks Cerebras plans to deploy; 10-Q says it expects to require significant additional capital.
Losses and NOLs (FY2025 tax $7.1M on pre-tax $244.9M driven by a non-operating gain) keep cash tax low until 2028; statutory 21% by FY2029.

Below CRWV trailing 23.5x, NVDA 27.0x (NVDA.ev_ebitda_ttm 27.2x) and TSM 19.5x because by 2029 growth slows to ~20%, ~70% of revenue depends on one customer whose MRA term (3-4 years, max 5) ends 2029-2030, and wafer-scale SRAM scaling has stalled.
Cost of equity 5.24% + 2.29 x 4.20% = 14.86%; debt (F6 $918M, OpenAI loan at 6%) ~2% of capital => WACC ~14.8%.

F7 net debt -$7,003.3M (debt $918.2M - cash $6,742.2M - ST investments $1,179.4M) less ~$680M restricted cash (press release: cash, equivalents, restricted cash and ST investments $8.6B - F1 - F2 $7,921.6M). Operating lease liabilities ($568.8M) not added because rent is in operating costs.

Class A 112.25M + Class B 111.60M + Class N 13.72M outstanding at 2026-08-05 (237.56M) + 27.22M options (2016-plan strikes $0.36-$13.01, treasury method ~26.1M) + 27.63M RSUs + 10.03M vested unexercised OpenAI warrant shares (4.46M Jan-2026 + 5.57M Jun-2026).

Remaining 23.4M of the 33.45M OpenAI warrant shares vest with capacity delivery; ~half by the horizon => ~+3.2%/yr. This is customer-warrant dilution (stands in for the non-cash contra-revenue excluded from core revenue), not SBC, which is costed in EBIT.

Peer forward P/S: NVDA 10.1x, AMD 14.4x, AVGO 10.8x, MRVL 14.5x, ALAB 20.7x, CRDO 12.3x, ARM 40.8x, ANET 17.7x, NBIS 7.65x, CRWV 2.2x (EV-based ~4.6x = EV $88.4B / ($42.4B/2.20)). Cerebras placed between the neocloud pair (4.6-7.65x) because most revenue is cloud capacity at ~40% core gross margin and NTM growth at the horizon (~+85%) then slows to ~20%.
Below neocloud CRWV trailing 23.5x and NVDA 27x; NTM EBITDA at horizon is still ramping, so a forward-on-forward multiple below trailing peer levels.

Bear: Nvidia Groq 3 LPX in full production (Nebius, CoreWeave first) and OpenAI reported to run a new Ultrafast tier on Nvidia GPUs; Bull: AWS Bedrock and AMD Helios partnerships plus OpenAI 1.25GW option.
